## 2

I understand why some images can seem hard to trust, especially when they come through institutions or the media. But the evidence for a round Earth doesn’t depend on space photos alone: ships disappear over the horizon from the bottom up, Earth’s shadow on the Moon during lunar eclipses is always curved, different stars are visible at different latitudes, and time zones follow naturally from a rotating globe. Satellites, GPS, long-distance aviation, and independent observations all rely on the same model. It’s reasonable to question evidence, but the flat-Earth explanation would require many unrelated observations and technologies to be faked or mistaken in exactly coordinated ways.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny molecules in the air. Blue light gets scattered in many directions more easily than red light, so blue light fills the sky around us. That’s why the sky looks blue when the Sun is high. At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, which scatters away much of the blue and leaves more red, orange, and pink light reaching our eyes.

雨从傍晚一直下到深夜，城市像被一层透明的纱幕笼住。昏黄的路灯映在积水里，随着水波轻轻晃动，仿佛碎了一地的月光。屋檐不断滴水，发出单调而安静的声响。偶尔有汽车驶过，轮胎卷起白雾，转眼又消失在巷口。窗边的人捧着一杯热茶，听雨声漫过夜色，心里那些白日里的喧闹，也慢慢沉了下来。
